---
title: "Whetstone"
subtitle: "Any skill that learns from use — and the proof it does."
---

**Whetstone** is a local [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that attaches to an existing
skill and lets it improve from ordinary use. When you correct the skill, Whetstone *captures* the
correction as a weighted **learning** (soft taste) or a mandatory **issue** (hard rule), and *recalls*
the relevant ones at the start of every later run — no separate review step, all committed to git.

## The one claim

> A correction the skill received once is **tracked** and keeps being **honored** on later runs.

This site proves that claim two ways, across three real skills —
[Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/) (data into publication-ready tables),
frontend design (self-contained web pages), and PowerPoint decks (python-pptx) — each taught its own
arbitrary house-style preference:

- **[See it](triptych.qmd)** — a *before* output (empty store), the *learned layer* the skill recalled
  in its own words, and the *after* output that applied it.
- **[Measure it](metrics.qmd)** — two honest metrics read straight from Whetstone's telemetry:
  **runs-to-stick** (how quickly a correction stopped needing to be repeated) and
  **value-over-time** (how a learning's weight held up across later runs).

There is no LLM judge grading "prettiness": the point is to show a correction is *tracked and
re-applied*, and to measure that directly. Every number links back to how it was produced on the
**[Methodology](methodology.qmd)** page.

```{python}
# | echo: false
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from _showcase import load_metrics, not_generated_note  # noqa: E402
from IPython.display import Markdown  # noqa: E402

m = load_metrics()
if m is None:
    out = not_generated_note("The headline numbers")
else:
    # Headline numbers span every skill — the full aggregate across great-tables, frontend-design,
    # and pptx (the same set the Before / After and Metrics pages show).
    a = m["aggregate"]
    n_skills = len(m.get("skills", {})) or 1
    out = Markdown(
        f"### At a glance\n\n"
        f"- **{a['preferences_stuck']} of {a['preferences_total']}** corrected preferences stuck "
        f"(consistently re-applied after correction).\n"
        f"- Median **runs-to-stick: {a['median_runs_to_stick']}**.\n"
        f"- Backend: `{m['backend']}` across **{a['scenarios']}** scenarios in "
        f"**{n_skills}** skills.\n"
    )
out
```

## Scope

v1 covers the **visual** skill class, demonstrated across three skills (Great Tables, frontend
design, and PowerPoint decks). The **code** and **context** classes — the same substrate applied to
a code-improvement skill and a context-organizing skill — are coming next.
